reviews.t: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Beard and Moustache Trimmer
reviews.x: I wonder if all these reviews are pertaining to this particular model, some reviews dont sound like my unit. I find no real problem with mine. Nothing is perfect. It is a bit bigger than my old small Wahl, but it has more features that require that. The vacumn works great, which alone makes my purchase of it worthwhile to me; in the past the sink always had a lot of nasty looking hairs all over it. Ive never had mine switch length setting on me, as some people describe, I dont see how it could.

reviews.t: It sucks. And that's a good thing!
reviews.x: I owned another Norelco beard trimmer with a vacuum in it ... until my wife broke it by knocking it off the shelf. But now I'm glad she did. On the old one, the vacuum was fairly useless because just as much hair ended up in the sink and all over the blade as in the catcher bin. Maybe more.  But the T980 Turbo (and don't all guys love stuff with "Turbo" in the description?) does the job. Yes, I know it has two settings: Turbo on and Turbo off. But I see no reason to use it with Turbo off because

I purchased this to replace a 3.5 year old Norelco T990 when its batteries died. I *loved* the T990 and would buy it again, but it's no longer available. (The current T765 is a similar design to the T990.) T980 issues: The electronic power and turbo switches are touch sensitive and too easy to press while trimming. The settings window is tiny and it's hard to read the number. The mini trimmer is an inconvenient attachment. When using the trimmer without the comb/guide, like for neck cleanup, the

reviews.t: Good, not great, with a flaw
reviews.x: The trimmer works pretty well.  It trims my beard and moustache adequately and to the length I want, but not on first pass.  Most of the trimmings make it into the collection chamber, but not all of them.  I would say about twenty percent of the trimmings end up in the sink not the collection chamber.  This is a replacement for me for a T990 Norelco trimmer, with a dead battery.  I now have to disassemble that trimmer to get at and remove the dead battery for recycling.  That is a problem with t

I also wonder if some of the negative reviews are for this particular model (Philips Norelco T980 for $39.99 @ Amazon).  -Does not feel cheap at all.  -Settings click into place.  They will change if you push it to the point where you think you would break it if you pushed any harder.  I dont see why anyone would need to push it that hard. I had to test it after reading some of the reviews.  -Turbo does not seem too loud at all.  -Vacuum works very well.

If you are considering getting this trimmer, all you need to know is this: The 9 lockable length settings don't actually lock!! I tried putting it on length "3", but when I started to trim, it went down to length "2".  Then I started on length 2 and it went down to length 1.  Besides this, the cutting block is too far away from the thing that touches your face (not sure what it's called), so it's very hard to cut any hair at all unless you choose the length setting 3 or lower. reviews.t: A Vacuum Trimmer that actually VACUUMS!!
reviews.x: I have owned two previous "accu-vac" models.  The vacuum always seemed kinda useless, mostly hype.  Well.....the "turbo" mode on this puppy REALLY vuccums!  If you can tolerate the noise that the turbo mode produces, I would recommend using turbo mode at all times.  If noise is a concern, like in early morning, the standard mode does an ok job too.  The price is right on this thing, and it LOOKS sweet.  95% mess free.  Very Nice!

First shave and my husband lost his short beard.  It shifted levels without him knowing it and left a racing strip. Needless to say he had to shave completely. Luckily he didn't trim his mustache. The vacuum works great but that's about it.

I've had a regular Norelco beard trimmer for years and when the battery would no longer hold a charge I decided to give this one a try.  I didn't really follow the vacuum or turbo descriptions but bought it anyway based on price.  Boy am I glad I did!  The vacuum makes trimming so much less of a mess.  I use it also to buzz cut my hair and there is virtually no mess now where there used to be stubbles of hair everywhere before.  I do have to empty the vacuum container a few times but less mess i
If you set it on level 5 and you push too hard, you may not have a beard. The locking system is a joke. The Norelco trimmer I bought 7 years ago has a better locking system.

I agree...with the negative reviews. I really like the guide on Norelco trimmers but that is about it for this latest model. I threw it away 2 days after I received it.  I practically shaved off my goatee after it switched from the 3 to the 1 setting by itself. The vacuum doesn't work all that well and if you travel, it is so easy to accidentaly turn this on as it just takes the slightest pressure on the switch to start it up. Bad news all around.

How in the world does this thing get 5 stars? The adjustable trimmer doesn't 'snap' when adjusting to number 2 trim. It also silently switches from trim number 3 - 2 if you press down hard enough. Also the blade has a 'shield' that aids in sucking the cut hair down into the collection chamber. The problem is the 'shield' blocks the head of the blade. Very dangerous if your cutting a line for your moustache-- your literally cutting blind. It does come with a cheap attachment for linings, but I pr

I like the concept of this trimmer with the vacuum and all, but I'm really annoyed that the people who make these things won't tell you what lengths the comb settings will trim to.  Even if you go to a store to look at one, they have it all sealed in plastic that you have to cut open just to take a look at it.  So I got this thing home to see if it would trim to my preferred length, and no it won't.  I'm liking the stubble look, and about 3-4 days growth looks best on me.  This trimmer only goes

reviews.t: Shifts beard length setting without warning
reviews.x: My T980 does almost everything perfectly: it holds a charge for weeks; its vacuum reduces the number of trimmed hairs around the sink by about 70%; it feels wonderful and it works quickly.  However, my T980 does NOT stay at the level I set it at. If I don't firmly grip the length setting wheel it will jump from, say, a 5 to a 3 -- as it did this morning -- embarrassing me either by giving me a patchy trim or by forcing me to shorten my beard length.  This problem doesn't seem to be a result of t

At first, people think this is some kinda sex-toy from the future. It's not. It's a beard trimmer. And a pretty good one to boot. If you're like me, you use your beard trimmer when you don't have much time in the morning before you have to take off for work. If you trim with this thing quickly on the 'normal' trimming mode, it'll catch maybe 75% of your hair in the vaccuum. However, when you enter warp speed (turbo mode) this thing is insane. It's really loud and sounds like it might explode, bu

My Norelco T900 was great, but broke recently, so I went out looking for another one, only to find it was discontinued. Didn't see any Norelco trimmers comparible to my old trimmer.  Bought a T980, took it home, and found out the first trim... its junk (I'm being nice with my wording).  Overall, its too big to easily hold.  Worst of all, the trim height setting moves when you press it against your face... so during my first trim, it ruined my goatee.  Not a good trimmer, period.  Too big, too mu

It seems fine for a battery operated trimmer, EXCEPT!  The trimmer doesn't stay at the setting you want.  So, I used it for the first time this AM, put the setting on 5 or 6, but after a few strokes on the beard, it reset itself to the lowest setting.  So, one spot on my beard is now down to a stubble.  So, I have to go ahead and shave the rest of my beard that short.  I tested it over and over, and slight pressure resets the length mechanism.  Long and short, the thing doesn't work.  I'm return

Unfortunately, Norelco really messed up what they had right to begin with. The length adjustment does not snap into place like my old Norelco trimmer and will shift while you are shaving. If you want to get a clean shave, go ahead and purchase this product, because that is exactly what you will have to do after using it. Disappointing build quality!

If you plan to travel outside the USA make sure you have a full charge and do not run out of juice while away. It is strange this day and age that products come with 110-120v transformers one vs. 110-240v; esp. personal care items like shavers and trimmers. If you run out of power when in Europe (say) plan to have to take a AC adapter or buy a new adapter while overseas. The trimmer works perfectly in every sense. The only thing that kills it is the fact that they decided to include an AC adapter that only works with 120 volts. In other words, if you travel, you can't charge this trimmer in most other countries. I don't think it's that much more expensive to include an adapter that accepts 110-230 volts. reviews.t: I hate shaving.  I LOVE THIS TRIMMER.
reviews.x: THIS THING IS AWESOME.  I AM NEVER SHAVING AGAIN. I just used it for the first time and have decided that I will never use a razor again.  I am a guy who never likes to shave, I maintain the "few days of stubble" look throughout the week, and dread the day when I have to go through the hassle of lathering up & shaving.  But this thing is so easy to use and it just cuts you down to whatever stubble-level you want in like 2 minutes!!!! PLUS it's got this vacuum-device on it that sucks up the stray

There have been a lot of complaints about the vacuum option of this trimmer.  Let's be realistic....its not a Hoover, it's a trimmer.  It catches MOST of the hairs, which is a lot better than NONE of the hairs.  I've used it a few times so far and haven't had the problem others complained about where the setting is changed mid-trim.  Just hold the thing below the dial, and not right on the dial.  It gave a nice even trim all around.  I've had it for a couple of months, used it 3-4 times, and sti

reviews.t: Norelco blew it with the vac/trimmer/guard interface.  This thing is bad.
reviews.x: I'm very disappointed with this trimmer. The thing that made me buy it is the thing that makes this unusable. I speak of the vacuum. It does a good job at keeping the hair out of the sink, but its placement sets the trimmer so far back from the guard that using this trimmer on setting 2 (which is what I always used on my old Norelco T7500 to keep it nice and tight) is the equivalent of setting 7 or so (which is fairly long) on my old trimmer so I am unable to get a nice tight, trim look. Bought this to replace an older model Norelco trimmer without a vacuum function.  Cuts well, I notice no problem with the height adjustment not staying locked in selected setting as others have mentioned.  Vacuum function definately works well.  I find it a little bit noisy in turbo mode.  My only complaint, and it's not really a complaint, is I did like the simplicity of my older model in just removing the hair comb to use the trimmer head for the detail work.  Because of the vacuum attachment

I got mine around three weeks ago.  The good news is that it cuts my beard well, and the vacuum is not noisy. claims.text: The vacuum feature works well and collects most trimmings, though some users note a portion still ends up in the sink.
The length settings do not lock reliably and can shift during use, sometimes resulting in unintended trimming.
The turbo mode provides strong vacuum suction but is noticeably noisy.
Some reviewers question whether negative reviews refer to this specific model and report no significant problems with their unit.
The touch-sensitive power and turbo switches are too easy to press accidentally.

qa.q: Does it cut close enough for a clean stubble look?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree: one user says it cuts down to whatever stubble level you want [3], but others say the lowest setting isn't short enough [4] and that the vacuum placement makes setting 2 cut like setting 7 [5].

claims.text: One user says it cuts down to whatever stubble level you want.
Another user says the lowest setting isn't short enough.
Another user says the vacuum placement makes setting 2 the equivalent of setting 7.

qa.q: How well does the vacuum actually catch the clippings?
qa.answer: Reviews report the vacuum catches most but not all clippings, with estimates ranging from about 75% in normal mode [2] to 80% collected (20% in the sink) [6], and one calling it 95% mess free [4]. Some praise it as working well [3][4], while one 1-star reviewer found the vacuum placement made the trimmer unusable [5].

claims.text: One reviewer estimates it catches about 75% of hair in normal mode [2].
Another says about 20% of trimmings end up in the sink rather than the collection chamber [6].
